kind: Emacs/Lisp live development client and RPC server

runtime.execution: Emacs frontend talks to SLYNK inside a long-lived Lisp; communication can use worker threads or single-thread styles.
runtime.service_boundary: Client consumes a Lisp runtime; SLYNK evaluates with that runtime authority.

summary: Addressed live evaluation, native compile/load, debugger restarts and inspectable recordings offer model-ergonomics ideas; this is not an agent loop.

inspection.scope: Read RPC dispatch/replies/authentication, eval/compile/load APIs, recordings and sticker tests.
inspection.limits: No complete backend-specific restart/interrupt review; no model provider, complete audit store or refit coordinator.

actions.name: interactive-eval / eval-and-grab-output
actions.output: Printed values, captured output or condition
actions.lifecycle: Persistent Lisp process; request continuation settles.

actions.name: compile-file-for-emacs / compile-string-for-emacs
actions.input: Path or source, load flag, source positions and policy

actions.name: :emacs-interrupt / :emacs-channel-send
actions.input: Thread or channel ID and message
actions.lifecycle: Independent connection dispatch; backend determines cancellation.

actions.name: compile-for-stickers
actions.output: Notes, armed state, later value/condition recordings

evidence.claim: Localhost default listener may accept multiple connections when configured.
Requests address threads and continuation IDs; interrupts and channel messages dispatch independently.
Evaluation is wrapped by configurable handlers and replies with ok/abort plus original continuation ID.
Interactive evaluation and output capture execute in the live Lisp environment.
Compile-file hook dispatch and compile-string return collected diagnostics and can load definitions.
Stickers record values/conditions/time in in-memory global vectors; source notes multiple-client limitation.

tests.focus: Instrumentation lifecycle after valid or invalid live compilation.
tests.oracle: Explicit ert-fail if compiled definitions do not arm selected stickers or invalid instrumentation arms any sticker; this is UI/instrumentation state, not raw audit completeness.

strengths: Thread and continuation identities make live evaluation/debugging inspectable.
Evaluation wrappers, diagnostics, object inspectors and restarts are strong ergonomic patterns.
limits: Runtime process and active stack lifetime remain backend-dependent.
Recordings are selective and in-memory; multi-client recording state is explicitly unfinished.
arconaut_questions: Which inspector/restart operations should the model use directly as ordinary programs?
How do we retain original IO while exposing curated debug recordings without confusing their scopes?
